title: How Dagobert Renouf grew Logology by sharing his real founder story on Twitter
summary: After 13 months averaging one user a week and failed paid channels, Dagobert went all-in on Twitter, sharing his struggles and memes. The community that formed recommended his product (even non-customers) and brought backlinks, partnerships and interviews. He also covers topic keywords, repurposing replies into tweets, and batch scheduling.

principles.text: Share your real struggles, not networking pitches; authentic vulnerability builds a community that recommends you.
principles.quote: the more vulnerable and authentic i am on twitter the stronger this community gets

principles.text: People who like you as a founder will recommend your product even if they never bought it.
principles.quote: nine out of 10 people who recommend it they never bought anything they just like me and what i'm doing

principles.text: Paid marketing doesn't substitute for hustle; you can't just pay money and get money without a lot of testing budget.
principles.quote: you can't just like pay money and then you make money like it's like i mean to get to that point you will need so much money to make testing

principles.text: Use the exact topic keywords in every tweet to get reach beyond your followers; the algorithm doesn't understand synonyms.
principles.quote: if you want to be trending in the marketing topic you need to use the word marketing

principles.text: Repurpose replies that did well into standalone posts; they act as an MVP proving the idea works.
principles.quote: it's kind of like you know an mvp for my tweets like oh people liked it so then i can repurpose as a stand-alone tweet

principles.text: One social channel done well compounds into backlinks, partnerships, interviews and credibility without extra effort.
principles.quote: i get about one new backlink every day doing nothing specific about it just from twitter
